events.text: The sibling project contains a useful piece earlier audits did not elevate: a full locally-connected/identity-component substrate for locally finite-type group schemes, including finite connected components. That can discharge the reducible algebraically-closed part of Stacks 39.8.6; I’m reading the exact public/private boundary now to see whether a small port can turn the current irreducible theorem into a componentwise theorem without importing unrelated Picard assumptions.

90	
    91	universe u
    92	
    93	open CategoryTheory Limits
    94	
    95	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    96	
    97	/-! ## §1. The identity component of a group scheme — abstract substrate
    98	
    99	The identity component is an abstract feature of `k`-group schemes locally of
   100	finite type. We package the definition + open-and-closed-subgroup-scheme
   101	structure in the `GroupScheme` namespace so they are reusable outside the
   102	Picard context.
   103	
   104	In this project, a "`k`-group scheme" is encoded as an
   105	`Over (Spec (.of k))`-object `G` carrying a `[GrpObj G]` instance (the
   106	group-object structure in the over-category). The locally-of-finite-type
   107	hypothesis is the `[LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom]` instance on the structural
   108	morphism to the base.
   109	
   110	Blueprint references: `def:identity_component_group_scheme` +
   111	`thm:identity_component_open_subgroup` (Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`). -/
   112	
   113	namespace GroupScheme
   114	
   115	/-- In a **Noetherian** topological space `α`, the set of connected
   116	components is finite.
   117	
   118	Proof: the map `irreducibleComponents α → ConnectedComponents α` sending each
   119	irreducible component `C` to the connected component of an arbitrary chosen
   120	point of `C` is well-defined (because `C` is preconnected, hence contained in
   121	a single connected component) and surjective (because every point lies in
   122	some irreducible component, namely `irreducibleComponent x`, which is a
   123	subset of `connectedComponent x`). The source is finite by
   124	`TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.finite_irreducibleComponents`, so the
   125	target is finite by `Finite.of_surjective`. -/
   126	private lemma noetherianSpace_finite_connectedComponents
   127	    {α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α] [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace α] :
   128	    Finite (ConnectedComponents α) := by
   129	  classical
   130	  have hfin : (irreducibleComponents α).Finite :=
   131	    TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.finite_irreducibleComponents
   132	  haveI : Finite ↥(irreducibleComponents α) := hfin.to_subtype
   133	  refine Finite.of_surjective
   134	    (fun C : ↥(irreducibleComponents α) =>
   135	      (ConnectedComponents.mk : α → ConnectedComponents α)
   136	        ((C.property : Maximal IsIrreducible C.val).prop.nonempty.some)) ?_
   137	  intro c
   138	  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := ConnectedComponents.surjective_coe c
   139	  refine ⟨⟨irreducibleComponent x, irreducibleComponent_mem_irreducibleComponents x⟩, ?_⟩
   140	  rw [ConnectedComponents.coe_eq_coe]
   141	  refine (connectedComponent_eq ?_).symm
   142	  exact irreducibleComponent_subset_connectedComponent
   143	    (isIrreducible_irreducibleComponent (x := x)).nonempty.some_mem
   144	
   145	/-- In a **Noetherian** topological space `α`, each connected component is
   146	open.
   147	
   148	Proof: `ConnectedComponents α` is totally disconnected
   149	(`ConnectedComponents.totallyDisconnectedSpace`), hence T1
   150	(`TotallyDisconnectedSpace.t1Space`), and finite by
   151	`noetherianSpace_finite_connectedComponents`. A finite T1 space is discrete
   152	(`Finite.instDiscreteTopology`), so the singleton
   153	`{ConnectedComponents.mk x}` is open in the quotient. The preimage of this
   154	singleton under the continuous quotient map `ConnectedComponents.mk` is
   155	`connectedComponent x` (`connectedComponents_preimage_singleton`), which is
   156	therefore open. -/
   157	private lemma noetherianSpace_isOpen_connectedComponent
   158	    {α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α] [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace α]
   159	    (x : α) :
   160	    IsOpen (connectedComponent x) := by
   161	  haveI : Finite (ConnectedComponents α) := noetherianSpace_finite_connectedComponents
   162	  haveI : DiscreteTopology (ConnectedComponents α) := inferInstance
   163	  have h := (isOpen_discrete
   164	    ({(ConnectedComponents.mk x : ConnectedComponents α)} : Set _)).preimage
   165	    ConnectedComponents.continuous_coe
   166	  rwa [connectedComponents_preimage_singleton] at h
   167	
   168	/-- The **`LocallyConnectedSpace` instance** for the underlying topological
   169	space of a `k`-scheme `G.left` whose structural morphism
   170	`G.hom : G.left ⟶ Spec k` is locally of finite type.
   171	
   172	The substantive content is EGA I 6.1.9: a locally Noetherian topological
   173	space has open connected components — equivalently, is locally connected.
   174	Pushed through the chain: `Spec k` is Noetherian (a field has Noetherian
   175	spectrum); `LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom + IsLocallyNoetherian (Spec k) ⟹
   176	IsLocallyNoetherian G.left` (Mathlib's
   177	`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian`); and the
   178	implication `IsLocallyNoetherian X ⟹ LocallyConnectedSpace X.toTopCat`
   179	comes from `noetherianSpace_finite_connectedComponents` together with
   180	`noetherianSpace_isOpen_connectedComponent` above.
   181	
   182	The classical proof: each point `y ∈ G.left` has an open affine
   183	neighbourhood `W = Spec R` with `R` Noetherian, hence `|W|` is a Noetherian
   184	topological space; in a Noetherian space, each `connectedComponent y` is
   185	clopen (finite irreducible components ⟹ finite connected components ⟹
   186	finite T1 quotient ⟹ discrete quotient ⟹ singletons clopen in quotient ⟹
   187	preimages clopen). Pulled back along the open inclusion `W ↪ G.left`,
   188	this gives an open connected neighbourhood of `y` inside any open `F`
   189	containing `y`. -/
   190	private instance identityComponent_locallyConnectedSpace
   191	    {k : Type u} [Field k]
   192	    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   193	    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
   194	    LocallyConnectedSpace G.left := by
   195	  haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian G.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian G.hom
   196	  rw [locallyConnectedSpace_iff_subsets_isOpen_isConnected]
   197	  intro x F hF
   198	  -- Extract an open neighbourhood `T ⊆ F` of `x`.
   199	  obtain ⟨T, hTF, hT, hxT⟩ := mem_nhds_iff.mp hF
   200	  -- Find an affine open `W ⊆ T` with `x ∈ W`.
   201	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hxW, hWT⟩ :=
   202	    exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (X := G.left) (U := ⟨T, hT⟩) hxT
   203	  haveI : IsNoetherianRing Γ(G.left, W) :=
   204	    IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian ⟨W, hW⟩
   205	  haveI hNoethW : TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace ↥W :=
   206	    noetherianSpace_of_isAffineOpen W hW
   207	  -- Inside `W` (Noetherian) the connected component of `x` is open; its image
   208	  -- under the open inclusion `W ↪ G.left` is the connected open neighbourhood
   209	  -- we want.
   210	  let xW : ↥W := ⟨x, hxW⟩
   211	  refine ⟨(Subtype.val : ↥W → G.left) '' connectedComponent xW, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   212	  · rintro _ ⟨z, _, rfl⟩
   213	    exact hTF (hWT z.2)
   214	  · exact W.isOpen.isOpenMap_subtype_val _
   215	      (noetherianSpace_isOpen_connectedComponent xW)
   216	  · exact ⟨xW, mem_connectedComponent, rfl⟩
   217	  · exact isConnected_connectedComponent.image _ continuous_subtype_val.continuousOn
   218	
   219	/-- The image of the identity section `e : Spec k → G` (well-defined as a
   220	single point of `|G|` because `Spec k` is a topological singleton). -/
   221	private noncomputable def identitySectionPoint
   222	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] : G.left :=
   223	  ((MonObj.one (X := G)).left.base :
   224	      ↥(Spec (.of k)) → G.left) (default : Spec (.of k))
   225	
   226	/-- The **clopen carrier `Set`** of the identity component of a `k`-group
   227	scheme `G` locally of finite type, packaged as a `G.left.Opens`.
   228	
   229	The carrier set is `connectedComponent x`
   230	for `x = e(*)` the image of the identity section
   231	(`identitySectionPoint G`); openness is `isOpen_connectedComponent` which
   232	needs the `identityComponent_locallyConnectedSpace` instance above
   233	(EGA I 6.1.9). -/
   234	private noncomputable def identityComponentCarrier {k : Type u} [Field k]
   235	    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   236	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
   237	    G.left.Opens :=
   238	  ⟨connectedComponent (identitySectionPoint G), isOpen_connectedComponent⟩
   239	
   240	/-- The identity component of `G` as an open subset of its underlying scheme.
   241	
   242	This is the public open-subscheme interface to the carrier used in
   243	`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent`.  Its underlying set is the topological
   244	connected component through the identity section. -/
   245	noncomputable def identityComponentOpens {k : Type u} [Field k]
   246	    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   247	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
   248	    G.left.Opens :=
   249	  identityComponentCarrier G
   250	
   251	@[simp]
   252	theorem coe_identityComponentOpens {k : Type u} [Field k]
   253	    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   254	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
   255	    (identityComponentOpens G : Set G.left) =
   256	      connectedComponent
   257	        (((MonObj.one (X := G)).left.base :
   258	          ↑(Spec (.of k)) → G.left) (default : Spec (.of k))) :=
   259	  rfl
   260	
   261	/-- The **identity component** `G^0` of a `k`-group scheme `G` locally of
   262	finite type.
   263	
   264	Encoded as a `k`-scheme: an object of `Over (Spec (.of k))`, carrying the
   265	intended substantive identity "this is the connected component of `|G|`
   266	containing the identity section `e`, equipped with the open-subscheme
   267	structure inherited from `G`". The associated open immersion
   268	`IdentityComponent G ⟶ G` is the content of
   269	`IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme`.
   270	
   271	Concretely, `IdentityComponent G` is built from `identityComponentCarrier G`:
   272	the open subscheme of `G` whose underlying topological space is the connected
   273	component of `|G|` through the image of the identity section, with the
   274	inherited structure morphism `(identityComponentCarrier G).ι ≫ G.hom`. The
   275	carrier is `connectedComponent (identitySectionPoint G)`, open by
   276	`isOpen_connectedComponent` under the
   277	`identityComponent_locallyConnectedSpace` instance (EGA I 6.1.9: locally
   278	Noetherian spaces have open connected components). -/
   279	noncomputable def IdentityComponent {k : Type u} [Field k]
   280	    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   281	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
   282	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   283	  Over.mk ((identityComponentCarrier G).ι ≫ G.hom)
   284	
   285	@[simp]
   286	theorem identityComponentOpens_toScheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
   287	    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   288	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
   289	    (identityComponentOpens G).toScheme = (IdentityComponent G).left :=
   290	  rfl
   291	
   292	/-- **The identity component is an open and closed subgroup scheme.**
   293	
   294	The bundled statement of Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`~(3): the identity
   295	component `G^0 = IdentityComponent G` of a `k`-group scheme `G` locally of
   296	finite type comes with a morphism `IdentityComponent G ⟶ G` (in
   297	`Over (Spec (.of k))`) whose underlying scheme morphism is both an open
   298	immersion and a closed immersion (i.e. the inclusion of a clopen
   299	subscheme).
   300	
   301	The remaining parts of Kleiman's conclusion — the group-subscheme property
   302	(the inclusion is a homomorphism of `k`-group schemes), finite-type-ness over
   303	`k` (`LocallyOfFiniteType` + quasi-compactness), geometric irreducibility and
   304	base-change-commutation — are stated separately as
   305	`IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism`,
   306	`IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible` and
   307	`IdentityComponent.baseChangeIso`.
   308	
   309	The inclusion morphism is `Over.homMk (identityComponentCarrier G).ι`, with
   310	the over-category compatibility holding by definition of
   311	`IdentityComponent G`. The `.left` of this morphism is
   312	`(identityComponentCarrier G).ι`, an open immersion by the global
   313	`Scheme.Opens.instIsOpenImmersionι` instance. For the closed-immersion
   314	half we apply `IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion` to the open immersion
   315	and reduce to `IsClosed (↑(identityComponentCarrier G) : Set _)`, which holds
   316	because the carrier is a connected component and connected components are
   317	closed. -/
   318	theorem IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
   319	    (G : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   320	    [GrpObj G] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] :
   321	    Nonempty {f : IdentityComponent G ⟶ G //
   322	        IsOpenImmersion f.left ∧ IsClosedImmersion f.left} := by

   803	/-- **EGA I 6.1.10** (topological form): a connected topological space in
   804	which every point admits an irreducible open neighbourhood is irreducible.
   805	
   806	Proof: let `Z` be the irreducible component of some point. For `z ∈ Z` pick
   807	an irreducible open `V ∋ z`; then `Z ∩ V` is nonempty, so
   808	`Z ⊆ closure (Z ∩ V) ⊆ closure V` (a nonempty open subset of a
   809	preirreducible set is dense in it); `closure V` is irreducible, so
   810	maximality of `Z` forces `closure V = Z`, whence `V ⊆ Z` and `Z` is open.
   811	Components are always closed, so the nonempty clopen `Z` is everything by
   812	connectedness. -/
   813	private lemma irreducibleSpace_of_connectedSpace_of_nhds
   814	    {α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α] [ConnectedSpace α]
   815	    (h : ∀ x : α, ∃ V : Set α, IsOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ IsIrreducible V) :
   816	    IrreducibleSpace α := by
   817	  obtain ⟨x₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
   818	  have hZmem : Maximal IsIrreducible (irreducibleComponent x₀) :=
   819	    irreducibleComponent_mem_irreducibleComponents x₀
   820	  have hZopen : IsOpen (irreducibleComponent x₀) := by
   821	    rw [isOpen_iff_mem_nhds]
   822	    intro z hz
   823	    obtain ⟨V, hVopen, hzV, hVirr⟩ := h z
   824	    have h1 : irreducibleComponent x₀ ⊆ closure V :=
   825	      (subset_closure_inter_of_isPreirreducible_of_isOpen hZmem.prop.2 hVopen
   826	        ⟨z, hz, hzV⟩).trans (closure_mono Set.inter_subset_right)
   827	    have h2 : closure V = irreducibleComponent x₀ :=
   828	      hZmem.eq_of_superset hVirr.closure h1
   829	    exact mem_nhds_iff.mpr ⟨V, h2 ▸ subset_closure, hVopen, hzV⟩
   830	  have hZuniv : irreducibleComponent x₀ = Set.univ :=
   831	    (isClopen_iff.mp ⟨isClosed_irreducibleComponent, hZopen⟩).resolve_left
   832	      (Set.Nonempty.ne_empty ⟨x₀, mem_irreducibleComponent⟩)

   837	type: it is the composite of the open immersion `G⁰ ↪ G` with `G.hom`. -/

   912	  have hg' : ∀ a, g'.left a = g := fun a => by simp [g', pointEquivClosedPoint]

import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FGAPicRepresentability
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GeometricallyConnectedSection
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivDegree
import AlgebraicJacobian.Genus

/-!
# The identity component of the Picard scheme

Let `G` be a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type. Its **identity
component** `G⁰` is the connected component of `|G|` containing the image of
the identity section. It is an open and closed subgroup scheme of `G`, of
finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`, and its formation
commutes with extension of the base field (Kleiman, §5, Lem.~`lem:agps`).

This file develops that substrate for an arbitrary `k`-group scheme (§1) and
then specialises it to the conditional legacy `PicSharp` representer
`PicScheme C` (§2). Section §3 contains only candidate integer maps at the
trivial legacy test object; it does not construct the arbitrary-test degree on
the étale-sheafified Picard functor. The corresponding degree-zero
characterisation in §4 remains open and is not faithfully typed by its legacy
approximation.

## Main results

- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` — the identity component
  `G⁰` of a `k`-group scheme `G` locally of finite type, as a `k`-scheme (an
  object of `Over (Spec k)`): the open subscheme of `G` carried by the
  connected component of the image of the identity section.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme` —
  the inclusion `G⁰ ↪ G` is both an open and a closed immersion.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism` —
  `G⁰` inherits the group-object structure of `G`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.baseChangeIso` — for a
  field extension `K/k`, the base change `(G⁰)_K` is isomorphic to `(G_K)⁰`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`
  — `G⁰` is of finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme` — the identity component
  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` of the Picard scheme.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.degree` — a conditional totalisation of
  an additive candidate at the legacy trivial test object, available only from
  `[ClassDegreePinned C]` and set arbitrarily to `0` off sections.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus` — the dimension of
  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is the genus of `C`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme.kPoints_iff_kerDegree` — the current
  conditional, typed-sorry approximation to the degree-zero characterisation;
  it is not an exact encoding of the classical statement on `k`-points.

The abelian-variety identification of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (smooth, proper,
geometrically irreducible `k`-group scheme of dimension `g(C)`) is assembled
in the sibling file `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`.

## Remaining obligations

The §1 substrate for an abstract `k`-group scheme is unconditional. The open
residues downstream of arbitrary-field étale Picard representability are
mathematically distinct:

- a genuine signed family degree: an additive natural transformation whose
  fibre value is `χ(C_t, L_t) - χ(C_t, O_{C_t})`, locally constant on arbitrary
  test schemes and invariant under the relative Picard quotient. The existing
  `ClassDegreePinned` interface does not provide these properties.
- `Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus`: the equality
  `dim Pic⁰_{C/k} = dim_k H¹(C, O_C) = g(C)`, which follows from
  Picard smoothness plus the tangent-space/dimension comparison. It does not
  depend on extracting a representing line bundle from a `k`-point.
- `Pic0Scheme.kPoints_iff_kerDegree`: the identification of the `k`-points of
  the legacy `Pic⁰_{C/k}` approximation with candidate-value-zero classes;
  its current type is not the arbitrary-field mathematical statement.

## References

- Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_IdentityComponent.tex`.
- Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5, Lem.~`lem:agps` (identity component
  substrate) + Prp.~`prp:pic0` (specialisation to `Pic_{C/k}`) +
  Thm.~`th:qpp&p` (quasi-projectivity/projectivity) + Cor.~`cor:sm`
  (smoothness/dimension) + Ex.~`ex:jac` + Rmk.~`rmk:Jac`
  (arXiv:math/0504020 pp. 36, 38, 47, 50–51);
- Milne, "Abelian Varieties" (course notes, 2008), §III.1
  (def. of abelian variety, p. 8; dimension equals genus, Rmk. III.1.4(e),
  p. 86).
-/

   783	force `CompactSpace` (`compactSpace_of_isProjective`), which `Pic_{C/k}` is not

   785	coproduct of components that each carry an H-quasi-projective witness.  Constructing
   786	those component witnesses is a separate producer obligation.

   788	`FiniteInAffine`, unlike `IsProjective` or `CompactSpace`, **is** closed under such
   789	coproducts: a finite set meets only finitely many components, each hit in an affine open,
   790	and finitely many disjoint affine opens have an affine `iSup`
